samples.summary: Backend maintenance scripts still attach to Yorkie with no auth token, so they 401 on any deployment where the webhook methods are registered
samples.evidence: This delta fixes the missing-token problem for `YorkieService` (`packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie.service.ts:74`) on the premise (yorkie-service-token.ts:9-12) that "with enforcement the default, a deployment that registers the webhook methods would 401 every one of those attaches, because an absent token is exactly what the webhook is there to refuse." The same premise applies verbatim to the three server-side Yorkie clients that do NOT go through `YorkieService` and were not given a token: `scripts/migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.ts:340` (`new yorkie.Client({ rpcAddr, apiKey })`), `scripts/migrate-yorkie-cf-ranges.ts:214`, and `scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts:204-210`. `YorkieAuthController.decide` verifies `body?.token ?? ''`, which throws, returning `UNAUTHENTICATED` (401) — so every attach in these migration/copy scripts is refused, and `copy-yorkie-documents.ts` will fail after `sourceClient.activate()`/`targetClient.activate()`. They fail loudly rather than corrupting data, hence minor, but the migration/copy tooling is unusable on an enforcing+registered deployment. `signYorkieServiceToken(secret, expiresIn)` is exported and DI-free precisely so these callers could use it, and none do.
searchedFor: Grep "from '@yorkie-js/sdk'" in packages/backend/src (only yorkie.service.ts constructs a client)
Grep 'authTokenInjector' across repo — no hits in packages/backend/scripts

samples.summary: New strict gate compares the raw env value without trimming or case-folding, unlike the reading it replaced, so `True` or a stray trailing space silently shuts the public gallery
samples.evidence: `assertYorkieAuthEnforced` now does `if (enforce === 'true') return;`, replacing `isYorkieAuthEnforced`, which normalizes with `raw?.trim().toLowerCase()` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:21). A `.env` / docker-compose value of `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true ` (trailing space is not stripped by dotenv-style quoting in every loader) or `TRUE` therefore fails the gate while the webhook itself reads the very same variable as enforcing, and the operator is told the deployment "requires YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true" when it is set to exactly that modulo whitespace/case. The failure direction is safe (gallery closed), so minor, but the two readings of one variable now disagree on inputs an operator will plausibly produce. `packages/backend/src/template/seed/register-templates.ts:157` duplicates the same untrimmed literal comparison, so the CLI inherits it.

samples.summary: The auth-token injector can throw synchronously despite being typed as returning a Promise
samples.evidence: `this.authTokenInjector = () => Promise.resolve(signYorkieServiceToken(secret, expiresIn));` evaluates `signYorkieServiceToken` before `Promise.resolve`, so a throw from `jsonwebtoken` (e.g. an operator setting `YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN` to a value `ms` cannot parse — the value is cast `as ms.StringValue` at line 52-54 with no validation) escapes synchronously from a function declared `() => Promise<string>` (line 37). Any SDK call site that does `injector().then(...)` outside a try block, rather than `await injector()`, would surface this as an uncaught synchronous error inside `client.activate()`/attach instead of a rejected attach. Wrapping the body in an `async` function (or try/catch) makes the failure a rejection as the type promises.
searchedFor: Glob for @yorkie-js/sdk sources (not present in the tree, so SDK call shape unverified)

samples.summary: Doc comment now misstates who shares this reading of the env var
samples.evidence: The header says this is "One reading of `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE`, shared by everything whose safety depends on it (the webhook itself, and the public template tier)." This delta removes both template-tier callers (`template-review.ts` no longer imports it; `register-templates.ts` compares the raw string), so the only remaining consumer is `yorkie-auth.controller.ts:133`. The comment now asserts a shared reading that the code deliberately no longer shares, which is exactly the confusion the new `assertYorkieAuthEnforced` docstring is trying to prevent.
